results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three main parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with parts in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body itself, with [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") subclasses of mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of mushroom body, and [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells, including gamma Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are several types of Kenyon cells, such as KCab-c(i), KCab-c, KCg-m, Kenyon cell of main calyx, and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes. Specifically, VFB holds [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") records for subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell, including [larval gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049827 "Open larval gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049830 "Open KCg-s in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049832 "Open KCg-s4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-t](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049833 "Open KCg-t in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-d](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110932 "Open KCg-d in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCg-m, KCg-s1, KCg-s2, KCg, and KCg-s3. VFB also has annotated data on gamma Kenyon cell, including available images, splits targeting gamma Kenyon cell, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, downstream connectivity classes, and upstream connectivity classes.

results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is connected to the mushroom body and lateral horn. results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as stated in the literature (Thomas and Wyman, 1984). According to VFB, it has specific anatomy, connectivity, genetic tools, and publications associated with it. The neuron has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center.

VFB holds various data related to the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. Additionally, VFB has annotated [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes for DNp01, which can be used to explore its connectivity. 

The connectivity of the giant fiber neuron can be described based on the available data. The downstream connectivity classes indicate the types of neurons or brain regions that the giant fiber neuron connects to, while the upstream connectivity classes indicate the types of neurons or brain regions that connect to the giant fiber neuron. 

For further information, relevant publications such as those by Koto et al. (1981), Power (1948), Thomas and Wyman (1984), Namiki et al. (2018), and Ito et al. (2014) can be consulted.
